data.paper_title: Profitability of Momentum Strategies: An Evaluation of Alternative Explanations
data.selected_experiment: Table 1, decile momentum portfolios formed on past six-month returns and held six months (NYSE/AMEX, 1965-1989, 1990-1997, 1965-1997), P1-P10 winner-minus-loser profit

economic_rationale.value: Momentum profits may reflect delayed overreaction/underreaction to information (behavioral models) rather than cross-sectional variation in expected returns; the paper tests whether JT momentum profits persist out of sample and evaluates these explanations.

evidence.quote: The behavioral models specify that the holding period returns arise because of a delayed overreaction to information that push the prices of winners (losers) above (below) their long-term values.

universe_and_filters.value: All NYSE/AMEX stocks, excluding NASDAQ stocks and excluding stocks priced below $5 at the beginning of the holding period

evidence.quote: We follow JT and include all NYSE/AMEX stocks and exclude NASDAQ stocks.
We also exclude all stocks priced below $5 at the beginning of the holding period.

signal_formula_words.value: Past six-month cumulative return of each stock over months -5 to 0, used to rank stocks into ten groups

evidence.quote: At the end of each month we rank the stocks in the sample based on their past six-month returns (month —5 to month 0) and then group the stocks into ten equally weighted portfolios based on these ranks.

At the end of each month we rank the stocks in the sample based on their past six-month returns (month —5 to month 0) and then group the stocks into ten equally weighted portfolios based on these ranks.

skip_window.value: none (holding begins in month 1 immediately after ranking month 0)

evidence.quote: Each portfolio is held for six months (month 1 to month 6) following the ranking month.

holding_period.value: 6 months (month 1 to month 6), with overlapping portfolios

evidence.quote: Each portfolio is held for six months (month 1 to month 6) following the ranking month.

rebalance_frequency.value: monthly (ranking at the end of each month; overlapping portfolios with each monthly cohort equally weighted)

evidence.quote: To increase the power of our tests we construct overlapping portfolios.

sort_rule_evidence.quote: At the end of each month we rank the stocks in the sample based on their past six-month returns (month —5 to month 0) and then group the stocks into ten equally weighted portfolios based on these ranks.

breakpoints.value: not stated; stocks are ranked on past six-month returns and grouped into ten portfolios, each with ten percent of the stocks

evidence.quote: P1 is the equal-weighted portfolio of ten percent of the stocks with the highest six-month lagged returns, P2 is the equal-weighted portfolio of the ten percent of the stocks with the next highest returns and so on.

favored_group.value: P1 (past winners: highest past six-month return decile)

evidence.quote: Portfolio P1 is comprised of stocks with the best ranking period returns and PlO is comprised of stocks with the worst ranking period returns.

disfavored_group.value: P10 (past losers: lowest past six-month return decile)

evidence.quote: Portfolio P1 is comprised of stocks with the best ranking period returns and PlO is comprised of stocks with the worst ranking period returns.

weighting_evidence.quote: At the end of each month we rank the stocks in the sample based on their past six-month returns (month —5 to month 0) and then group the stocks into ten equally weighted portfolios based on these ranks.

expected_sign_evidence.quote: The difference between the P1 and PlO portfolio returns is 1.11% per month, which is reliably different from zero.6

headline_result.value: Winner-minus-loser (P1-P10) return of 1.11% per month in 1965-1989 (t=4.61), 1.01% in 1990-1997, and 1.09% over 1965-1997 (t=5.65)

evidence.quote: In this more recent period, past winners outperform past losers by 1.01% per month, which is very close to the corresponding returns in the original JT sample period.

unresolved_details: Exact breakpoints for the decile cuts (e.g., NYSE-only vs all stocks) are not stated beyond ten percent of stocks per portfolio
Whether returns are simple or log returns is not stated
Treatment of delisting returns and minimum return history requirements not stated
Precise definition of the beginning-of-holding-period price for the $5 screen in overlapping portfolios not detailed
Signal formula given only in words; no explicit equation for the decile strategy
